title: Redwood + NovaTech MSA/DPA & SLAs review
summary: Review of MSA + DPA redlines, SLA targets, pricing approval path and onboarding timeline. Customer requests clarification on data residency, audit logs, and escalation for incidents. Agreement to send redline summary and security package; schedule procurement sign-off next week.
action_items: Samir - send consolidated redline summary and updated quote by 2026-04-02
Clara - provide mini-benchmark (p99/latency) for NovaTech expected workload by 2026-04-03
Ethan Park - send list of non-negotiable legal clauses by 2026-04-01
Maya Lopez - confirm procurement timeline and approvers by 2026-04-06
next_steps: Redwood to share security pack (SOC2 report, DPA, encryption/KMS details)
Redwood to send updated MSA with proposed concessions and a clean DPA
Schedule procurement review with finance + legal next Tuesday 2026-04-06 10:00 PT
Run short POC: 2 week pilot with dedicated capacity (optional) - scope to be defined
transcript:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to allocate about fifty, fifty five minutes to walk through the MSA and DPA redlines and talk slas and onboarding. um clara and i are on from product and solutions, who do we have from nova?
[00:08] Maya (NovaTech): hi, hi this is maya, i am head of procurement, and we have ethan from legal, jordan our cto, aisha our sre and liam product. thanks for doing this.
[00:15] Samir: perfect, appreciated. quick agenda: high-level commercial and pricing status, call out redlines in the MSA, DPA specifics (retention, residency, delete-on-demand), slas and support model, and then next steps for procurement.
[00:29] Ethan (NovaTech): real quick can you confirm recorded, and is there a deck?
[00:32] Samir: yes recorded, deck sent in calendar invite link, and we'll drop the security pack after the call.
[00:36] Clara (Redwood SE): quick note on the technical side \u0014 we can support hosted api, dedicated pools and private (vpc) installs, and for the pilot we usually recommend dedicated to match production latencies.
[00:46] Jordan (NovaTech): question: we had a redline about data residency. in the dpa you mention multi-region backups, we need EU-only. is that possible?
[00:54] Clara: yes, we offer region pinning on our private and dedicated offerings. hosted api is global but you can request region controls for data at rest, and we have options to restrict backups to eu regions \u0014 there may be a small price delta.
[01:07] Aisha (NovaTech SRE): and audit logs, does the private control plane expose per-request audit logs with keys for user mapping? we need proof for our auditors.
[01:15] Samir: yes, audit logs are included in the private package; for dedicated we can provide higher retention windows as an add-on. logs include request ids, model used, route, token counts, and role if passed. we'll include a sample schema in the security pack.
[01:28] Ethan: on the legal redlines \u0014 we've flagged the indemnification and liability caps, also termination language with regard to consumer data \u0014 we want 60 days notice for termination for convenience.
[01:36] Samir: i saw those, thanks. our standard is 30 days for convenience in hosted, 60 for enterprise private \u0014 we can propose a compromise: 45 days on the MSA for NovaTech, and carveouts for active investigations.
[01:48] Ethan: appreciate that, can you put that in the updated MSA?
[01:50] Samir: yes we'll put it in the updated MSA.
[01:52] Liam (NovaTech): pricing \u0014 our finance needs a clear path for approval, the quote you sent has committed vs on-demand lines, can you explain the committed discount thresholds and what triggers the reserved capacity?
[02:02] Clara: sure, committed is a monthly reserved capacity with a committed spend which unlocks discounts \u0014 we support burst capacity so you can go over in bursts but sustained overage will be billed at on-demand rates. typical thresholds in the quote are 10k, 50k, 150k tokens per month with increasing discounts.
[02:16] Jordan: latency slas \u0014 we saw p99 numbers in your catalog but our traffic profile is short chat-like calls (avg 80 tokens) we care about tail latency. can you commit to p99 under 300ms for the dedicated plan?
[02:30] Clara: phew, 300ms p99 is aggressive for GPU inference depending on model and token sizes. for smaller models it's workable; for larger ones we'll need batching tradeoffs. we can commit to 300-500ms p99 for dedicated small models, and we can run the pilot to validate with your workload.
[02:46] Jordan: okay pilot then.
[02:48] Maya: procurement question \u0014 do you have a standard procurement flow? we need an MSA that legal signs, then dpa and order form, and final sign-off by finance. timeline is roughly two weeks after legal ack.
[02:57] Samir: standard flow yes: sign MSA + DPA, order form for reserved capacity, then onboarding kickoff. we can expedite if we get approvals earlier.
[03:04] Ethan: another redline is data deletion \u0014 can you support verified deletion and certificate that backups are purged?
[03:10] Clara: we have a documented deletion flow; for private deployments it's customer controlled, for hosted we provide deletion APIs and retention windows. full backup purge needs a retention window plus a backup purge operation that can be validated \u0014 we'll include the deletion certificate process in the security pack.
[03:24] [00:03:30] Samir: and encryption \u0014 we do encryption at rest and transit by default; we support customer-managed keys (kms/hsm) in private and dedicated tiers.
[03:33] Aisha: SSO and role-based access \u0014 we use OKTA and want enforcement of scim + sso.
[03:38] Samir: supported; we have sso with saml/okta and scim provisioning, and can set up roles and restrict who can see logs.
[03:44] Liam: question about support and escalation \u0014 we need a named sla owner and 24x7 on-call for sev1. what are your sev definitions and ttr?
[03:52] Clara: our enterprise SLA includes 24x7 support with sev1 response within 30 minutes and p1 mitigation within 4 hours; we can include a named escalation contact and weekly reporting.
[04:03] Ethan: we will likely push for credits on downtime \u0014 what is your outage credit model?
[04:07] Samir: standard outage credits based on downtime percentage, up to a capped percent of monthly fee \u0014 specifics in SLA appendix, we can propose a slightly higher credit for dedicated reserved customers.
[04:18] Jordan: on onboarding, how long to get dedicated capacity up and running?
[04:21] Clara: typical is 7-14 business days for dedicated after order form and bill setup; private vpc can be 3-6 weeks depending on networking approvals.
[04:32] Maya: procurement needs an estimated schedule to present to execs. can you give a high level?
[04:36] Samir: sure: week 0 \u0014 sign MSA/DPA and order form; week 1 \u0014 kick off onboarding and access; week 1-2 \u0014 dedicated cluster provisioned and baseline tests; week 3 \u0014 pilot run and final tuning; week 4 \u0014 go-live for initial routes. we'll put that in the onboarding plan.
[04:52] [00:04:55] Ethan: are there any subprocessor lists? we want to see vendor list for backups and infra.
[05:00] Samir: yes subprocessor list included in the DPA appendix; we will provide current list and a notification process for changes.
[05:07] Aisha: monitoring integrations \u0014 we want prometheus metrics and trace hooks into our datadog. is that possible?
[05:12] Clara: yes we have prometheus endpoints and tracing hooks, and we can forward metrics to your datadog org with an integration token.
[05:20] Liam: can you give sample numbers for token-based billing if we hit 100k tokens/day? want to show finance the monthly burn.
[05:26] Samir: quick calc \u0014 at the committed discount tier in your quote 100k tokens/day ~ 3M tokens/month, at discount rate it is approx $Xk per month (we'll put exact numbers in an updated quote).
[05:36] Maya: on the MSA, there were several ambiguous sections about service credits and force majeure. can you tighten language?
[05:41] Samir: yes we'll tighten. we'll circulate a redline and a clean version.
[05:45] Ethan: legal also wants archive retention limits and disposition process for logs older than 90 days \u0014 we don't want logs kept indefinitely.
[05:52] Clara: we can set retention windows and auto-delete after X days, and for private deployments that can be configured by you.
[05:59] [00:06:05] Jordan: for the pilot, what models will we run? are you bringing your own or using open models?
[06:12] Clara: we recommend starting with a mid-sized open model that matches your latency needs; we can also test a quantized variant to reduce cost.
[06:19] Jordan: ok low-risk approach.
[06:21] Samir: quick callouts on procurement path \u0014 finance usually wants a PO or order form, then billing setup. if you need CA/NDAs we can push earlier but for now MSA + DPA + order form is enough.
[06:34] Maya: final question on approvals \u0014 who needs to approve final pricing?
[06:37] Samir: typically the finance lead and procurement \u0014 if you want we can do a joint session with your finance team and our pricing manager.
[06:45] Maya: please do that.
[06:47] Samir: great, i'll send calendar for next tuesday.
[06:50] Ethan: one more legal point \u0014 we need to ensure data processing subcontracts are auditable. can you provide evidence of third party audits?
[06:57] Samir: we'll include SOC2 report and list of third-party auditors in the security pack.
[07:03] Clara: i'll also attach a mini-benchmark with sample p50/p90/p99 for short-chat traffic, and tweak configs for kv cache so you see tail improvement.
[07:12] Aisha: for incident response, we need a commitment to root cause analysis within 7 business days for sev2/sev1.
[07:18] Samir: we can commit to postmortem within 10 business days standard, but we'll aim for 7 for sev1 in the enterprise SLA.
[07:26] Maya: ok to recap next steps?
[07:29] Samir: sure. clara will send the benchamrk, i'll send redline summary and updated quote and security pack, ethan will send must-have legal clauses, maya will confirm procurement timeline and approvers. we'll set the procurement review next tuesday at 10am PT.
[07:43] Liam: tiny typo \u0014 benchamrk is spelt wrong in chat but fine.
[07:46] Samir: lol thanks, noted.
[07:48] Jordan: last note on fallback \u0014 if dedicated capacity hits limits do you have automatic fallbacks to hosted for burst?
[07:55] Clara: yes you can configure smart routing to fallback to a compatible model in hosted if capacity constrained, and we can set cost controls.
[08:05] Maya: thanks all, good productive call.
[08:09] Samir: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and calendar invite.
[08:13] [END]
